REPORT questions[1] says (B) 'seems to fail generically' in open subsets of Minkowski space, and gives as the reason 'a bounded I⁻(x, W) cannot hold an unbounded Cauchy surface'. That reason covers only W whose Cauchy surfaces are unbounded. For bounded W (a diamond) (B) also fails, but because of particle horizons: a vertical line near the edge starts above x. The question is hedged and claims nothing about the paper, so it is not a finding.

Name nit, not a finding: Causal.minkowski_zero_ext (:308) reads like an ext lemma at the zero vector. It is the statement that a point of ℝ^{1,0} is determined by its time. A name such as minkowski_zero_eq_of_fst_eq would be clearer, but the current one causes no clash.
